correctness.rationale: For the specified labelled thirty-vertex cubic bipartite incidence graph, every radius-three ball leaves eight antipodal vertices. Complete local layer-intersection table bounds subsequent radius-two, radius-one and singleton coverage by four, two and one, proving maximum at most 29 even for illegal tuples. Equality requires each bound sharp. Duad first-source case split enumerates 6 distance-two choices with 2 admissible synthemes and 2 last choices (24), plus 8 distance-four choices with 3 synthemes and 2 last choices (48): 72 per first source. A verified involutive incidence automorphism exchanges the two halves; six-label permutations ensure all 30 vertices equivalent. Hence 2160 total, 720/1440 by second distance, 9 per each of 240 first-source/survivor antipodal pairs. All equality cases satisfy ignition-separation inequalities. Five pairwise distance-four duad ignitions cover all vertices, giving burning number 5. Both standalone implementations were executed from their original source paths, independently reconstruct graph and all 810000 ordered four-tuples, agreeing on entire equality census; Python checks 900 local pair intersections and explicit polarity. Finite enumeration is exhaustive for this graph and is not asserted to generalize.

originality.rationale: The nearest original and expanded works define graph burning, ball covers, radius bound and studied host families, but do not state or imply the exact Tutte–Coxeter four-round near-covering classification. A broad survey, same-host graph geometry literature, searches for cage aliases and indexed exact calculations were checked at statement/implication level. The new claim is not merely that this graph has radius four or burning number five: it includes a sharp nonlegal-safe coverage obstruction and a complete antipodal 2160-tuple equality census. value.rationale: Tutte's eight-cage is the canonical smallest cubic girth-eight graph, whose generalized-quadrangle distance shells give a natural near-covering experiment at four burning rounds. The theorem discovers and explains a sharp obstruction: every four-source schedule misses at least one vertex, with 2160 distinct equality sequences and a uniform nine sequences for each antipodal survivor. The structural two-orbit equality split is mathematically motivated by its distance-regular geometry and provides precise finite-horizon diffusion information not implied by the graph's diameter, ordinary radius bound or known metric-basis counts. This is a complete natural finite classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice; only this graph and the standard burning process are claimed.
